scope: Corollary 8.1 (Complete hyperbolic surfaces of genus zero) of the manuscript “Koebe's Circle-Domain Conjecture” (preprints/Koebes-Circle-Domain-Conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 071 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f0080bd36e38b2cd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 61. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let S be a connected orientable surface without boundary, of genus zero, and let g be a complete Riemannian metric on S with Gaussian curvature identically −1. There is a compact set Y ⊂ ∂∞H3, containing at least three points, whose complement is nonempty and connected, such that every connected component of Y is a closed round disk or a singleton and (S, dg) is isometric to ∂C(Y ) with its intrinsic path metric. When C(Y ) is two-dimensional, ∂C(Y ) denotes the metric double of C(Y ) across its relative boundary in the containing totally geodesic plane. Surfaces are understood to be Hausdorff and second countable; their number of ends is unrestricted.
